and N‑Allenyl Benzimidazoles by Pd- or Bi-Catalyzed Direct
N‑Alkenylation Reactions
Guodong Shen,* Kun Bi, Dehe Wang, Zhirong Zhao, Xuan Tang, Xianqiang Huang,* and Xin Lv*

ABSTRACT: We have developed a condition-controlled divergent synthesis of (Z)-N-vinyl and N-allenyl benzimidazoles from
1,1,3-triphenylprop-2-yn-1-ols and benzimidazoles through Pd- or Bi-catalyzed N-alkenylation reactions involving nucleophilic attack
and C−C bond cleavage processes. The desired two different kinds of products can be conveniently and selectively synthesized by
using this strategy, which features stereospecific synthesis, good functional group tolerance, a broad substrate scope, and high
efficiency. The strategy provides significant advantages for the synthesis of biologically and pharmaceutically active
imidazoheterocycles.
■
INTRODUCTION
Benzimidazoles
1
and allenes
2
are two important classes of
organic frameworks and are widely found in natural
compounds, pharmaceuticals, organic intermediates, and
materials science due to their unique biological activities and
physical properties. For example, as shown in Figure 1, N-vinyl
benzimidazoles (A) and (B) exhibit potent PPARc partial
agonistic activity and modest PPARa agonistic activity.
3
R-
Cytallene (C) and R-adenallene (D) are inhibitors of HIV and
hepatitis B replication.
4
The natural product peridinin (E) is
the main light-absorbing pigment in peridinin-chlorophyll α-
protein (PCP), and its unique structure significantly alters the
character of excited states.
5
However, new types of function-
alized N-allenyl benzimidazoles, which possess potential
research values, have very few relevant reports.
6
Therefore,
the synthesis of N-vinyl and N-allenyl benzimidazoles holds
certain research significance.
Metal-catalyzed N-alkenylation is a prominent method for
C−N bond formation,
7
serving as an efficient strategy for the
direct and precise synthesis of organic nitrogen-containing
intermediates.
8
Over the past decades, numerous metal
catalytic systems have been explored.
9
Recently, Kikuchi and
Yoshikai and co-workers reported N-alkenylation reactions of
azoles, alkynes, and iodine(III) electrophiles for the synthesis
of N-vinylazoles.
10
Anderson and co-workers developed a gold-
catalyzed N-alkenylation of isoxazolines to synthesize N-vinyl
gold intermediates for further derivatization.
11
The direct N-
alkenylation of benzimidazoles has been achieved and obtained
good results,
12
but there are relatively few reports on N-
alkylation catalyzed by bismuth metal. Herein, seeking new
catalytic reactions to assemble various functionalized (Z)-N-
vinylbenzimidazoles with economically accessible starting
materials is still very meaningful (Scheme 1).
13
Considering
the significant advances in the functionalization of allenes and
benzimidazoles, it would be meaningful for the convenient
assembly of new N-allenyl benzimidazoles.
The metal-catalyzed nucleophilic attack and C−C bond
cleavage processes can efficiently facilitate the N-alkenylation
reaction.
14
By involving metal catalysis, nucleophilic attack
reactions proceed mildly and efficiently, leading to the
formation of C−N bonds.
15
Additionally, metal-catalyzed C−
C bond cleavage has emerged as an exceptionally efficient and
powerful method for breaking inert and thermodynamically
stable C−C bonds.
16
This reaction can participate in numerous
subsequent transformations and maintain high regioselectivity

17
Furthermore, propargylic alcohol
chemistry is a powerful tool for constructing various complex

18
Herein, as a continuation of our
previous works, we reported a condition-controlled strategy
for the selective synthesis of (Z)-N-vinyl and N-allenyl
benzimidazoles from 1,1,3-triphenylprop-2-yn-1-ols and benzi-
midazoles through Pd- or Bi-catalyzed N-alkenylation reactions
via nucleophilic attack and C−C bond cleavage processes.
■
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Initially, we searched for suitable conditions for the synthesis
of 1-(1,3,3-triphenylpropa-1,2-dien-1-yl)-1H-benzo[d]-
imidazole 1c using 1,1,3-triphenyl-2-acetyl-1-ol 1a and
benzimidazole 1b as the model substrates (Table 1). The
reaction was carried out with Yb(OTf)
3
as the catalyst in DCE
at 120 °C for 24 h. The anticipated product 1c was isolated in
a 33% yield (Table 1, entry 1). We screened different Lewis
acids, and Bi(OTf)
3
was the best choice (Table 1, entries 1−
6). Next, different solvents were tested (DMSO, CHCl
3
,
MeCN, DMF, and DCE), and the use of DCE afforded the
highest yield (Table 1, entries 5 and 7−10). When 1.2 equiv of
1a was used, the yield increased significantly (Table 1, entry
11). To our delight, the product was obtained in good yield
when 13X molecular sieve (80 mg) was used, indicating that
anhydrous conditions are important for the reaction (Table 1,
entry 12). At the same time, we also carried out the gram-level
experiment, and the reaction yield did not change (80%, 0.61g;
Table 1, entry 12). We used Cu(OTf)
2
as a catalyst to replace
Bi(OTf)
3
under the best conditions (Table 1, entry 13), and
1c was isolated in 42%. Without the catalyst, no product was
detected (Table 1, entry 14).
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, some
representative substrates were selected to explore the scope of
this transformation (Table 2). First, we evaluated the influence
of substituted benzimidazoles b. The yields decreased when
substrates bearing electron-withdrawing functional groups
were employed (Table 2, 1c−5c). Interestingly, when 7-
methyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole was used to do the reaction,
only 4-methyl-1-(1,3,3-triphenylpropa-1,2-dien-1-yl)-1H-
benzo[d]imidazole 2c was isolated for the steric effect. The
HMBC confirmed the structure of 2c (for, see ESI, Figures S3
and S4). The reactions of 2-methyl and 2-phenyl benzimida-
zoles proceeded smoothly, and the corresponding products
were isolated in moderate to good yields (Table 2, 6c−7c).
The electronic effect of R

isolated for the electronic effect (Table 2, 4c). However, the

The HMBC confirmed the structure of 2d (for, see ESI,

these results, it could be found that the reaction was also
influenced by the electronic effect, and R
3

with
electron-donating functional groups were more favorable for
the reaction. For the Pd-catalyzed N-alkenylation reactions via
nucleophilic addition and C−C bond cleavage processes, no
(E)-products were observed during the synthesis, indicating
the advantages of this method for efficient stereospecific
synthesis.
We conducted several control experiments that could
support the mechanisms of the reactions (Scheme 2). First,
1a was transformed to benzophenone 1h and 1,4-diphenylbu-
ta-1,3-diyne 1i under the optimal reaction conditions for the
synthesis of 1d (eq 1). Then, phenylacetylene 1e and 1b were
also reacted under the optimal conditions, and only (E)-1-
styryl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole 1f was isolated in 70% yield (eq
2), which confirmed the Pd-catalyzed nucleophilic addition
and C−C bond cleavage processes. Finally, deuterated DMF
was used as the reaction solvent, and 1d was detected without
deuterated H in 75% yield (eq 3), excluding the proton
exchange from DMF during the reaction.
Based on experimental observation and related literature,
19
the mechanisms are proposed in Scheme 3. For N-allenyl
benzimidazoles, intermediate 1aa was formed by the
coordination of Bi(OTf)
3
with 1a. Then, 1b could react with
1aa to form intermediate 1ab by nucleophilic attack reaction,
and 1c was produced from intermediate 1ab by the elimination
of Bi(OTf)
3
and H
2
O. For the synthesis of (Z)-N-vinyl
benzimidazoles, organometallic intermediate 1ac could be
formed first; 1ad was obtained by the nucleophilic addition
reaction of 1ac with 1bb, which was formed via 1b and Base.
After the transmetalation and protonolysis processes, 1ad was
transferred to 1ae and 1af. Intermediate 1ag was produced by
the C−C bond cleavage process, and 1d was obtained in the
present of BaseH
+
. When comparing the two reactions, the
formation of the five-membered ring intermediate 1ad of the
palladium-catalyzed reaction was stable, so 1bb attacked the
alkynyl carbon near the hydroxyl group. The Bi(III) catalyst
probably only plays a coordination role and promotes hydroxyl
departure. The electronic effect makes the phenyl-linked
alkynyl carbon more electrophilic, favoring nucleophilic attack.
■
CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed Pd- or Bi-catalyzed N-
alkenylation reactions for the selective synthesis of (Z)-N-vinyl
and N-allenyl benzimidazoles from 1,1,3-triphenylprop-2-yn-1-
ols and benzimidazoles via nucleophilic attack and C−C bond
cleavage processes. The reactions exhibit good stereoselectiv-
ity, broad functional group tolerance, and good yields, and a
wide variety of (Z)-N-vinyl and N-allenyl benzimidazoles were
obtained. The importance of these substituted benzimidazoles
would make the approach very attractive for biological and
pharmaceutical applications.
